exposure: Residence/SES dyads (rural/high SES, rural/low SES, urban/high SES, urban/low SES)
cohort: 9606 adolescent mothers (aged 15-19) with singleton, live deliveries registered in the Alberta Perinatal Health Program between 2010 and 2015
finding: Rural pregnant adolescents of low SES had the highest odds of adverse pregnancy outcomes compared to urban adolescents of high SES.
mod_finding: Rural/low SES adolescent mothers had increased odds of operative vaginal delivery and Caesarean section compared to urban/high SES mothers.
